Header: Colletotricum lindemuthianum In Sinhala: “Pulli rogaya”; In Tamil “Bonchi kai aluhal”

Prevention: Do a crop rotation with cabbage, tomato, potato etc.
Remove and destroy crop debris of previous season
Do proper land preparation (deep plough to bury remained crop residues)
Use disease-free seeds (avoid seeds with brown/ black lesions)
Do not re-use stakes previously used in infected fields
Use recommended fertilizers (do not apply additional doses of
Nitrogen fertilizer) which improve the crop vigour
Monitoring: Early in the season, look for brown/ black lesions along the veins of underside of mature leaves
In 1-11/2 month old crop, brown/red lesions develop on vines of infected plants
After pod setting, typical anthracnose symptoms (brown/black sunken lesions) can be seen on pods
Pink colour conidial masses can be seen on infected parts under humid conditions
Pod infection results the formation of brown/black lesions on seeds
If leaf and vine symptoms exceed 5% level during rainy season (October- February) go for chemical control
Direct Control: Do not wet the foliage during irrigation (do furrow or surface irrigation)
If possible, remove and destroy heavily infected leaves during early part of crop growth
Collect infected pods at harvesting and destroy or bury them
Restrictions: Chlorothalonil at the early stage of crop growth; During rainy season, apply a systemic chemical in between 2-3 applications of
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use); Contact

II (Moderately hazardous); Systemic; Application intervals 14-21 days; Do not apply more than 2 sprays/crop; Overdose and repeat spray will adversely effect crop growth and yield; Do not use after flowering
II, Systemic; Do not use after flowering
III (Slightly hazardous); Systemic; Do not use after flowering
III; Systemic; Do not use after flowering
